issue: Does the bar in 28 U.S.C. § 2244(b)(1) on re-presenting a claim from a prior application apply to second or successive motions for federal postconviction relief under 28 U.S.C. § 2255?

sides.position: Section 2244(b)(1) applies to second or successive § 2255 motions, so a claim already presented in a prior application must be dismissed.
cases: Winarske v. United States, 913 F.3d 765 (8th Cir. 2019)

sides.position: Section 2244(b)(1) does not apply to second or successive § 2255 motions; such motions are analyzed only under the gateway provisions of § 2255(h).
cases: Jones v. United States, No. 20-71862 (9th Cir. 2022)

this_court: does not apply § 2244(b)(1) to second or successive § 2255 motions; analyzes them under § 2255(h) instead, which aligns it with the Sixth Circuit
quote: This court has not yet decided whether the bar in § 2244(b)(1) applies to second or successive § 2255 motions, and our sister circuits are divided on the matter.
cite: Willie Jones, Sr. v. United States, No. 20-71862 (9th Cir. 2022)
